The Steelmen[http://www.footballcrests.com/clubs/motherwell-fc Motherwell F.C. ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512021059/http://www.footballcrests.com/clubs/motherwell-fc |date=12 May 2017 }}, ''Football Crests'' | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1886|5|17}}{{harvnb|Wilson|2008|p=86}} | ground = [[Fir Park]][http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/the-club/fir-park/ Fir Park] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410122813/http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/the-club/fir-park/ |date=10 April 2017 }}, ''Stadium on Motherwell FC Website'' | capacity = {{SPFL-stadiums|motherwell}} | chairman = Kyrk Macmillan | manager = [[Alfred Johansson (football manager)|Alfred Johansson]] | league = {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} | season = {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe2}} | position = {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe3}} | website = {{URL|http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk}} | pattern_la1 = _motherwell2627h | pattern_b1 = _motherwell2627h | pattern_ra1 = _motherwell2627h | pattern_sh1 = _motherwell2627h | pattern_so1 = _motherwell2627hl | leftarm1 = FFBE00 | body1 = FFBE00 | rightarm1 = FFBE00 | shorts1 = ffffff | socks1 =FFBE00 | pattern_la2 = _motherwell2627a | pattern_b2 = _motherwell2627a | pattern_ra2 = _motherwell2627a | pattern_sh2 = _motherwell2627a | pattern_so2 = _motherwell2627al | leftarm2 = 9e0000 | body2 = 9e0000 | rightarm2 = 9e0000 | shorts2 = 9e0000 | socks2 = 9e0000 | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | current = 2026–27 Motherwell F.C. season }} '''Motherwell Football Club''' is a Scottish professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Motherwell]], [[North Lanarkshire]], which plays in the {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}}. Motherwell have not dropped out of the top flight of Scottish football since 1985, and have lifted one trophy in that time – the [[Scottish Cup]] [[1991 Scottish Cup final|in 1991]].{{cite web|title=Motherwell 4 – 3 Dundee United|url=http://progs.fairlyoriginal.com/motherwell-4-3-dundee-united|work=fairleyoriginal.com|access-date=3 September 2012|archive-date=4 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504001021/http://progs.fairlyoriginal.com/motherwell-4-3-dundee-united|url-status=live}} Owing to the town's history of steel production, the club is nicknamed '''"the Steelmen"'''; or "the Well" for short. Clad in their traditional claret and amber, Motherwell play their home matches at [[Fir Park]] and have done so since 1896. The club's main rivals over the years have been [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], due in part to their close geographical proximities. These matches are known as the [[Lanarkshire derby]]. The club have won four major trophies in domestic football: the [[List of Scottish football champions|Scottish League title]] in [[1931–32 Scottish Division One|1931–32]], the [[Scottish Cup]] in [[1952 Scottish Cup final|1951–52]] and [[1991 Scottish Cup final|1990–91]], and the [[Scottish League Cup]] in [[1950 Scottish League Cup final|1950–51]]. ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' has suggested Motherwell's fans as the originators of the "[[Viking Thunder Clap]]", a supporting chant eventually popularised by the fans of the [[Iceland national football team]], where fans stay silent and let out loud synchronised claps seconds apart, gradually speeding up; the chant received wider international attention during [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]].{{cite magazine |last1=West |first1=Jenna |title=What Does Iceland's Skol Viking Clap Mean? |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/06/15/iceland-skol-clap-meaning-explained-world-cup-history |access-date=6 July 2020 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |publisher=ABG-SI LLC |date=15 June 2018 |archive-date=6 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706044815/https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/06/15/iceland-skol-clap-meaning-explained-world-cup-history|url-status=live }} ==History== ===Beginnings=== Motherwell was born on 17 May 1886, when representatives of the two main Motherwell works teams Glencairn FC and [[Alpha F.C.]] met in Baillie's pub in the town's Merry Street, and decided to merge the two teams with the aim of creating a club to represent the town as a whole at a higher footballing level. Motherwell's debut fixture proved to be a successful one as they overcame [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] 3–2.{{harvnb|Wilson|2009|p=20}} [[File:Motherwell FC League Performance.svg|thumb|right|Yearly table positions of Motherwell in the League.]]The early years proved somewhat chaotic as the club had little regular competition to play in, and matches would often start with players short, as men failed to turn up on time after their shifts in the local ironworks. On 5 August 1893, the decision was made to turn professional,{{harvnb|Wilson|2008|p=116}} and the club was consequently elected to the league, then being the only Lanarkshire side to compete at national level.{{harvnb|Wilson|2008|p=118}} Up until 1895, the club had played at a few different venues, including a site at Roman Road, and [[Dalziel Park (stadium)|Dalziel Park]]. The small pitch and muddy conditions at Dalziel Park were deemed unsuitable and [[Baron Hamilton of Dalzell|Lord Hamilton]] granted a lease on a plot of land on his Dalzell estate. This new ground was named [[Fir Park]] and has remained the club's home for over 120 years. The following years saw the club grow, appointing their first and longest serving manager to date, John 'Sailor' Hunter, who would go on to steer the club into its most successful period. In 1913, the decision was made to change the club's colours from blue to the now signature claret and amber. It is thought this was inspired by the success of [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], who also sport claret and amber, although a more romantic version of events claims them to have been Lord Hamilton of Dalzell's racing colours.{{cite web|title=1886–1917|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/the-club/history/club-history/1886-1917/|work=Motherwell FC Official Club History|access-date=9 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120129121248/http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/the-club/history/club-history/1886-1917/|archive-date=29 January 2012|url-status=dead}} ===1920s and 1930s successes=== [[File:Argentina motherwellfc 1928.jpg|thumb|160px|Motherwell playing [[Argentina national football team|Argentina national team]] at [[Boca Juniors]] stadium, 1928]] Motherwell enjoyed a successful period in the aftermath of [[World War I]], managed by [[John Hunter (footballer, born 1878)|John Hunter]]. The club placed third in the [[1919–20 Scottish Football League|1919–20 season]] and, although narrowly avoiding relegation in [[1924–25 Scottish Division One|1924–25]], they steadily climbed the table and enjoyed seven successive seasons finishing in the top three. In the summer of 1927, the club made a very successful tour of Spain, winning six out of the eight games they played and losing only one. These results included an emphatic 3–1 victory over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and a 2–2 draw with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].{{harvnb|Wilson|2009|p=36}} Following their success in Spain, the club went on another [[British football clubs tours to South America|summer tour, this time of South America]].[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53403363 Motherwell: Beating Argentina & bringing football to South America] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207190849/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53403363 |date=7 February 2021 }}, BBC Sport, 16 July 2020 After losing only three of their previous ten games, the tour culminated in a 5–0 defeat by a Brazilian League Select side.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/motherwell-satrip28.html South American Trip of Motherwell FC 1928] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404150836/https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/motherwell-satrip28.html |date=4 April 2023 }}, [[RSSSF]] Motherwell's first (and to this day, only) Scottish League championship came in [[1931–32 Scottish Division One|1931–32]] – with 30 wins in 38 fixtures, scoring 119 goals – a record 52 of which were scored by [[Willie MacFadyen]], who remains to this day the record holder for most goals scored in a single season and one of the club's all-time top goalscorers with 251 goals.{{harvnb|Wilson|2009|p=35}} The championship was sealed on 23 April 1932, when [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] could only draw at home against [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], handing Motherwell the title without kicking a ball.{{harvnb|Wilson|2008|p=72}} Between 1904 and 1947, this was also the only League title won by a club outside the Old Firm.{{Cite web |date=2018-03-26 |title=Old Firm's enduring appeal |url=https://www.fifa.com/news/y=2009/m=2/news=old-firm-enduring-appeal-1023776.html |access-date=2023-06-07 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613234603/https://www.fifa.com/news/y=2009/m=2/news=old-firm-enduring-appeal-1023776.html |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=game online |url=https://www.payeindehol.com/ |access-date=7 June 2023 |archive-date=7 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607070525/https://www.payeindehol.com/ |url-status=live }} In the two seasons following the league title win ([[1933–34 Scottish Division One|1933–34]] and [[1934–35 Scottish Division One|1934–35]]), 'Well finished runners-up, as they had also been in [[1926–27 Scottish Division One|1926–27]] and [[1929–30 Scottish Division One|1929–30]]. They also contested three Scottish Cup finals in this period – in [[1930–31 Scottish Cup|1931]], [[1932–33 Scottish Cup|1933]] and [[1938–39 Scottish Cup|1939]], but lost them all. ===Post-World War II period=== Following the break-up of the squad after [[World War II]], the club were not instantly successful. It then captured two major trophies in as many years with victories in the [[1950 Scottish League Cup final]] and the [[1951–52 Scottish Cup#Final|1952 Scottish Cup Final]]. The club was then relegated for the first time ever at the end of the [[1952–53 in Scottish football|1952–53 season]], but the club were promoted the next year. Following their return to the First Division, [[Bobby Ancell]] took management of the club in 1955 and presided over an era in which highly regarded [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] stars including [[Ian St John]] and Charlie Aitken played for the club.{{Cite web|url=http://qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=976|title=QosFC: Bobby Ancell|access-date=1 January 2012|archive-date=17 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617131849/http://qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=976|url-status=live}} However, Motherwell were unable to keep their assets, and no trophies were won in Ancell's era. His resignation came in 1965 amidst a downturn in form which eventually saw the club relegated back to the Second Division at the conclusion of the [[1967–68 in Scottish football|1967–68 season]]. ===1970s recovery and the McLean era=== Motherwell were immediately promoted back to the First Division in [[1968–69 in Scottish football|1969]], maintaining a mid-table position. The 18-team First Division was superseded by a new 10-team Premier League for the [[1975–76 in Scottish football|1975–76 season]], at which time they were managed by [[Willie McLean (footballer, born 1935)|Willie McLean]] and his assistant [[Craig Brown (footballer born 1940)|Craig Brown]] (who would become manager almost 35 years later). Under their management, Motherwell improved to fourth in the table with players such as Bobby Graham, Willie Pettigrew and Bobby Watson. The most notable cup run of that period was the [[1975–76 Scottish Cup]] where they eliminated Celtic and lost out in the semi-final to Rangers. ===1980 and 90s=== [[File:1991 Scottish Cup Win tribute - geograph.org.uk - 3125303.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tribute to Motherwell's 1991 Scottish Cup winning side]] Relegation down to the now-First Division and promotion back to the Premier League occurred twice in the early 1980s, before a decade under manager [[Tommy McLean]] (brother of Willie) culminated in a Scottish Cup win in [[1990–91 in Scottish football|1991]]. However, similarly to the Ancell era, Scotland internationalist [[Tom Boyd (Scottish footballer)|Tom Boyd]] was sold in the close season after the cup win. Results faded for two years before reaching another two season zenith immediately following the signing of [[Paul Lambert]] with third ([[1993–94 in Scottish football|1993–94]]) and second-placed ([[1994–95 in Scottish football|1994–95]]) Premier League finishes. The 1995 runners-up finish was the club's highest finish since [[1933–34 in Scottish football|1933–34]]. With Tommy McLean's departure to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in 1994, much of his squad was broken up; a large fee in particular was paid by [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for [[Phil O'Donnell (footballer)|Phil O'Donnell]]. Much of this money was reinvested in the squad, while the club cycled through managers including [[Alex McLeish]] and [[Harri Kampman]]. At this point, in August 1998, John Boyle bought the club, taking over from John Chapman.{{harvnb|Wilson|2008|p=120}} [[Billy Davies]] was appointed as manager, and large transfer fees were paid for prominent players including ex-Scotland internationals [[John Spencer (Scottish footballer)|John Spencer]] and [[Andy Goram]]. The investment though failed to provide results on the pitch. ===2000–2009=== By the end of Davies' tenure the club were in financial trouble. [[Eric Black]] was briefly in charge with the club floating near the foot of the table before it was placed in [[Administration (law)|administration]] in April 2002 with losses approaching [[Pound sterling|GBP]] 2 million yearly.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/scotland/1948121.stm "Motherwell in turmoil"] BBC Sport, 24 April 2002 Black resigned, and was replaced by [[Terry Butcher]]. The club's outlook remained bleak as they were forced to make redundant or release 19 players and replace them with younger players; Boyle also placed the club up for sale.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/motherwell/1958230.stm "Motherwell axe 19 players"] BBC Sport, 29 April 2002 Relegation in [[2002–03 in Scottish football|2002–03]] – normally automatic following a last-place finish in the league – was avoided on a technicality, as First Division winners [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] lacked a stadium meeting Premier League regulations.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/f/falkirk/2931808.stm "Falkirk denied promotion"] BBC Sport, 23 May 2003 [[File:Fir Park, Motherwell. - geograph.org.uk - 219204.jpg|thumb|right|[[Fir Park]], home of Motherwell]] Despite the lack of resources, a number of young talented players were found to play for the club; crucially, when many of these moved on, including [[Stephen Pearson]] and [[James McFadden]], they brought revenue in the form of transfer fees, and with John Boyle waiving the club's personal debt to him, its financial future was assured by the conclusion of the [[2004–05 in Scottish football|2004–05 season]] with the club's yearly losses falling to one of the lowest figures in the Premier League[http://worldsoccer.about.com/b/a/140198.htm "Scottish Soccer Clubs Still In Debt"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051216094606/http://worldsoccer.about.com/b/a/140198.htm |date=16 December 2005 }} [[World Soccer Magazine|World Soccer]], 18 January 2005 and the club coming out of administration in time to avoid a ten-point Premier League penalty which was being phased in for teams in administration.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/motherwell/3433979.stm "Motherwell plans still on course"] BBC Sport, 27 January 2004 On the field, the club also managed to reach the [[2005 Scottish League Cup final|League Cup final]], although they were comprehensively defeated by Rangers. Butcher moved on to [[Sydney FC]] at the end of the [[2005–06 in Scottish football|2005–06 season]], and was succeeded by his assistant Maurice Malpas. Malpas' stint at the club lasted just one season before his resignation in May 2007. After a short period with [[Scott Leitch]] as [[caretaker manager]], [[Mark McGhee]] was appointed to the position.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/motherwell/6761427.stm McGhee named new Motherwell boss] BBC Sport, 18 June 2007 In his first season as manager, McGhee would take the club to third in the league, and thus qualify for the UEFA Cup for the first time in 13 years, where they would be beaten by French side [[AS Nancy Lorraine|Nancy]] 3–0 on aggregate.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7639449.stm | work=BBC News | first=Thomas | last=McGuigan | title=Motherwell 0–2 AS Nancy (0–3) | date=2 October 2008 | access-date=8 September 2010 | archive-date=26 July 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726104846/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7639449.stm | url-status=live }} Mark McGhee left Motherwell for the vacant managerial position at [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in June 2009, and was replaced by [[Jim Gannon]]. Former [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] manager [[Craig Brown (footballer born 1940)|Craig Brown]] took over when Gannon left. ===2010–present=== Brown helped the club finish fifth in the SPL and qualify for Europe. The 2010–11 season saw the club in the Europa League and they defeated [[Breiðablik (men's football)|Breiðablik]]{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8842400.stm | work=BBC News | title=Breidablik 0–1 Motherwell (0–2) | date=22 July 2010 | access-date=4 September 2010 | archive-date=26 July 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726104841/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8842400.stm | url-status=live }} and [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesunds]]{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8879281.stm | work=BBC News | title=Motherwell 3–0 Aalesunds FK (4–1) | date=5 August 2010 | access-date=27 August 2010 | archive-date=11 December 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211070358/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/8879281.stm | url-status=live }} before losing in the Play-off round to [[Odense Boldklub|Odense]]{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8944768.stm | work=BBC News | title=Motherwell 0–1 Odense (agg 1–3) | date=26 August 2010 | access-date=5 September 2010 | archive-date=24 September 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924021154/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/8944768.stm | url-status=live }} preventing them from reaching the group stages of the competition. Brown left Motherwell for Aberdeen on 10 December 2010.{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/aberdeen/9257495.stm|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|title=Aberdeen name Craig Brown as new manager at Pittodrie|date=10 December 2010|access-date=10 December 2010|archive-date=10 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101210045020/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/a/aberdeen/9257495.stm|url-status=live}} [[Stuart McCall]] was named as his successor. This season saw the club reach the [[2010–11 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] Final where they were defeated 3–0 by Celtic.{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_cups/9491542.stm | work=BBC News | first=Martin | last=Conaghan | title=Motherwell 0–3 Celtic | date=21 May 2011 | access-date=17 October 2013 | archive-date=22 May 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522112815/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_cups/9491542.stm | url-status=live }} The 2011–12 season saw Motherwell reach the qualifying round of the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] for the first time. They finished third, one place outside the normal two spots allocated to the SPL for the Champions League. However the club was awarded a place because the club that had finished above them, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], went into administration and were prevented by UEFA from playing in European competitions. In the draw for the third qualification round of the Champions League, Motherwell were drawn against Greek heavyweights [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathanaikos]]. This ended in disappointment, as Motherwell were knocked out after losing 2–0 at home and then 3–0 away.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18964891|title=Motherwell 0-2 Panathinaikos|work=BBC Sport |date=30 July 2012 |access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=26 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726104922/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/18964891|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19074400|title=Panathin'kos 3-0 Motherwell (5-0)|work=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2012 |access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=22 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171022104720/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19074400|url-status=live}} The 2012–13 season brought even greater success in the SPL as the club finished second in the table{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/match/index.html?event=21;season=2012/13|title=Football Game Scores – Football Scoreboard – ESPN|access-date=26 August 2016|archive-date=20 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020124348/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/match/index.html?event=21;season=2012%2F13|url-status=live}} and once again qualified for the [[Europa League]]. It also saw striker [[Michael Higdon]] win the [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]] award.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22424675|title=Higdon named player of the year|work=BBC Sport |date=6 May 2013 |access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803005049/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22424675|url-status=live}} Goalkeeper [[Darren Randolph]] ([[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Premier League 6|second year running]]), defender [[Shaun Hutchinson]] and midfielder [[Nicky Law (footballer, born 1988)|Nicky Law]] were selected for the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Premier League 7|PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4522/kenya/2013/05/02/3948172/wanyama-makes-spl-team-of-the-season|title=Wanyama makes SPL team of the season - Goal.com|date=2 May 2013|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=9 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109034246/http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4522/kenya/2013/05/02/3948172/wanyama-makes-spl-team-of-the-season|url-status=live}} {{wide image|Motherwell v Dundee Utd.png|900px|A panoramic view of Fir Park, pictured during a Scottish Premiership fixture between Motherwell and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].}} Motherwell were granted associate membership of the [[European Club Association]] in June 2013, becoming the fifth Scottish club to join the Association. The club were invited to join after consistent qualification for European competition between 2008 and 2013.[http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2013/06/25/motherwell-join-the-eca/ Motherwell join the ECA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227181315/http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2013/06/25/motherwell-join-the-eca/ |date=27 December 2013 }} motherwellfc.co.uk. 25 June 2013. Retrieved 27 December 2013. In the 2013–14 season, Motherwell were knocked out of the Europa League by Russian side [[FC Kuban Krasnodar|Kuban Krasnodar]] 3–0 on aggregate in the third qualifying round.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23527518|title=Kuban 1-0 Motherwell (agg 3-0)|work=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2013 |access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=5 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170205212012/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23527518|url-status=live}} On 22 January 2014, Motherwell won their 40th Lanarkshire cup beating Hamilton Academical 1–0, thanks to a 54th-minute goal by 19-year-old youngster Jack Leitch. On the final day of the [[2013–14 Scottish Premiership]], Motherwell won 1–0 at [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] with a dramatic 93rd-minute winner, leapfrogging Aberdeen in the process to seal a second successive runners-up spot in the league.[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/living-high-life---well-3540604 Living the high life – Well dramatically finish second] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514182147/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/living-high-life---well-3540604 |date=14 May 2014 }} Daily Record. 14 May 2014. It was a season that also saw a first ever competitive defeat to [[Lanarkshire]] neighbours [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]], sitting third bottom of [[2013–14 Scottish League Two|Scottish League Two]] at the time, 1–0 in the [[2013–14 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]].[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25064081 Albion Rovers 2–1 Motherwell] BBC Sport. (2021), ''The Greenock Murders'', published by mybestseller.co.uk. ==Records and statistics== {{See also|List of Motherwell F.C. records and statistics||List of Motherwell F.C. players}} The club has won four major trophies in its history: the First Division in 1931–32, the Scottish Cup in 1952 and 1991, and the Scottish League Cup in 1950. In addition, it has won the second-tier Scottish league on four occasions; as the Second Division in [[1953–54 in Scottish football|1953–54]] and [[1968–69 in Scottish football|1968–69]], and as the First Division (beneath the Premier League) in [[1981–82 in Scottish football|1981–82]] and [[1984–85 in Scottish football|1984–85]]. They also won the [[SuperCupNI|Milk Cup]] in 1983, and the Scottish Summer Cup in 1944 and 1965. [[Bob Ferrier (English footballer)|Bob Ferrier]] holds the record for the number of Motherwell appearances, with 626 in the inter-war period. The goalscoring record is held by [[Hughie Ferguson]], who scored 284 league goals in 10 seasons in the 1910s and 1920s. [[Willie MacFadyen]]'s 52 goals in the title-winning 1931–32 season remains a club (and country) record for goals in one season. The club's record European appearance holder is [[Steven Hammell]], with 19 appearances for the club in Europe. The current record European goalscorer is [[Jamie Murphy (footballer, born 1989)|Jamie Murphy]], with seven goals. Also, the 8–1 win over [[Flamurtari FC|Flamurtari]] on 23 July 2009 currently stands as their record victory in European competition.{{cite news | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/8164957.stm | title = Motherwell 8–1 Flamurtari | date = 23 July 2009 | publisher = BBC Sport | access-date = 24 July 2009 | archive-date = 9 October 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201009014451/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8164957.stm/ | url-status = live }} Fir Park's current safety certificate limits the capacity to 13,742, [[All-seater stadium|all-seated]] in accordance with the [[Taylor Report]], although the ground is listed as {{SPFL-stadiums|motherwell}}.{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/clubs/motherwell/ |title=Motherwell Football Club |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |access-date=30 September 2013 |archive-date=6 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170506192825/http://spfl.co.uk/clubs/motherwell/ |url-status=live }} Its average home gate for the [[2018–19 Motherwell F.C. season|2018–19 season]] was 5,448. and cups in their history, which includes four major domestic trophy successes. Their sole [[List of Scottish football champions|Scottish league championship]] came in season [[1931–32 Scottish Division One|1931–32]] (finishing with 66 points in total, a winning margin of 5 points). Their biggest cup success was winning the [[Scottish Cup]] twice in [[1951–52 Scottish Cup|1951–52]] (4–0 v [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]) and [[1990–91 Scottish Cup|1990–91]] (4–3 v [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]), and the [[Scottish League Cup]] once in [[1950–51 in Scottish football|1950–51]] (3–0 v [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]). Motherwell also won the now defunct [[Summer Cup (Scotland)|Summer Cup]] in 1943–44 and 1964–65. They have also won the [[List of winners of the Scottish Championship and predecessors|second tier]] of Scottish league football on four occasions. Other notable cup success includes winning the [[Scottish Qualifying Cup]] once and winning the [[Lanarkshire Cup]] forty times, most recently in its last edition played in 2014. Their most recent cup final appearances came in the [[2017–18 Scottish Cup]] and the [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup]], losing both to Celtic 2–0. Their best league performance recently in the Scottish top flight was registering back-to-back second-place finishes in [[2012–13 Scottish Premier League|2012–13]] and [[2013–14 Scottish Premiership|2013–14]]. They have qualified for [[UEFA competitions|European competition]] ten times.
